body_ar:
السؤال : مال موقف الشرع من الاستنساخ الجيني للخلايا البشرية الذي أثير مؤخراً؟

الإجابة: إن الله سبحانه وتعالى جعل في الرحم مبيضين كل واحد منهما ينتج بويضة، فإذا أنتج أحدهما هذا الشهر لم ينتج الآخر وينتج الآخر في الشهر الذي يليه وهكذا بالتناوب، وإذا نتجت البويضة وتكاملت تنزل من المبيض إلى أحد عنقي الرحم فتكون قابلة للتلقيح، فإذا لقحت بإذن الله في تلك الفترة حصل حمل والله تعالى وحده، هو الذي يعلم ما كان من ذلك نفساً مخلقة وما كان غير مخلقة، سواء حصل هذا التلقيح بالطريقة العادية، أو وقع عن طريق التلقيح الصناعي سواء كان ذلك بالأنابيب أو بشق البويضة وتلقيحها بأية خلية أخرى، ولهذا فإن ذلك لا يغير شيئاً من خلق الله، لكن الله إنما شرع التلقيح بالطرق المعتادة .

وهذا النوع الذي يقصد به التدخل في خلق الله وتغيير خلق الله وإكساب بعض الصفات الوراثية ومنع بعضها محرم شرعاً بالأولى من الوشم والوشر والتنمص، فكل ذلك تغيير لخلق الله حرام، ويلعن فاعله، فكذلك من فعل هذا فهو ملعون لأنه سعى في تغيير خلق الله.
body_en:
The question: What is the position of the Sharia on the genetic cloning of human cells that has been raised recently?

The answer: God, glorified and exalted, placed in the womb two ovaries, each one of which produces an ovum. If one of them produces in this month, the other does not produce, and the other produces in the month that follows, and so on by turns. When the ovum is produced and is complete, it descends from the ovary to one of the two necks of the womb and becomes receptive to fertilisation. If it is fertilised, by God's leave, in that period, a pregnancy comes about — and God the Exalted alone is the One who knows which of that is a formed soul and which is unformed — whether this fertilisation comes about in the ordinary way, or occurs by way of artificial fertilisation, whether that be by test tubes or by splitting the ovum and fertilising it with any other cell. For this reason, that does not change anything of God's creation; but God has prescribed fertilisation only by the customary means.

As for this kind, the purpose of which is to interfere in God's creation and to alter God's creation, and to confer certain hereditary characteristics and to prevent others — that is forbidden (ḥarām) in the Sharia a fortiori, by comparison with tattooing, the filing of the teeth and the plucking of the eyebrows; for all of that is an alteration of God's creation and is forbidden, and the one who does it is cursed. So likewise, whoever does this is accursed, because he has striven to alter God's creation.

flags.arabic: محرم شرعاً بالأولى من الوشم والوشر والتنمص … ويلعن فاعله، فكذلك من فعل هذا فهو ملعون
flags.context: the ruling in the second paragraph
options: forbidden a fortiori, and the one who does it is accursed
forbidden by priority of reasoning, and the doer falls under the curse mentioned in the report
forbidden, and the doer is cursed
flags.note: EDITORIAL, and the highest-risk sentence in the record. بالأولى is the uṣūl argument a fortiori (qiyās al-awlā): the Sheikh reasons from the three practices cursed in a well-known prophetic report — tattooing, filing the teeth, plucking the eyebrows — to the greater case. The English must keep the reasoning chain visible (style guide section 1) and must not present the conclusion bare. The word ملعون, 'accursed', is applied to a person who performs genetic modification; in English, out of context, that reads as a religious condemnation of named classes of scientist and clinician, and this record sits in a bioethics area regulated in every Western jurisdiction. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened. The Sheikh gives no report reference and none has been added.

flags.arabic: ولهذا فإن ذلك لا يغير شيئاً من خلق الله، لكن الله إنما شرع التلقيح بالطرق المعتادة
flags.context: the end of the first paragraph, on IVF and on fertilising a split ovum
options: that does not change anything of God's creation; but God has prescribed fertilisation only by the customary means
that alters nothing of God's creation, though God has legislated fertilisation only in the usual ways
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The two paragraphs draw a distinction that any excerpt will destroy. The first says that assisted fertilisation, including by test tube or by splitting and fertilising an ovum, alters nothing of God's creation — while adding that God prescribed the customary means. The second forbids what is INTENDED to alter creation and to select hereditary traits. The record must never be displayed as a flat ruling that cloning or assisted reproduction is forbidden; the object of the prohibition is the intent to modify. The first clause also stops short of saying assisted fertilisation is permitted, and the English must not supply that conclusion either — style guide section 6.

flags.arabic: ما كان من ذلك نفساً مخلقة وما كان غير مخلقة
options: which of that is a formed soul and which is unformed
which of it is a fully formed creation and which is not
what of it is shaped and what unshaped
flags.note: The wording مخلقة وغير مخلقة is that of Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:5, but the Sheikh does not quote the verse or cite it, so it has not been set in the Qur'anic quotation braces and no reference has been added. 'Formed' is the usual rendering of mukhallaqah in that verse; the alternatives are recorded because the term carries weight in discussions of the beginning of life.

flags.context: the physiological description opening the answer
options: placed in the womb two ovaries
placed in the reproductive system two ovaries
flags.note: SOURCE, recorded not corrected (house rule 11). The Arabic says the two ovaries are 'in the womb', and describes the ovum descending 'to one of the two necks of the womb'. This is not the anatomy of modern medicine, and the description of strict monthly alternation between the ovaries is likewise a simplification. It is translated exactly as given, without an anatomical gloss and without correction; the reasoning that follows does not depend on it.

options: read as ما موقف الشرع, 'what is the position of the Sharia'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11), minor: مال is a run-together of ما and a stray lām, or a typing slip for ما. Read by the evident sense; body_ar preserves the source.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: The record is 900 characters and is a complete fatwa with a question and a ruling. On a character-count test it would have passed, but it is worth stating that it was classified by the presence of an answer, not by length.

الوشر is the filing or sharpening of the teeth, التنمص the plucking of the eyebrows; both are named in the prophetic report underlying the a fortiori argument, and the English names them plainly rather than transliterating.

الاستنساخ الجيني is rendered 'genetic cloning' throughout, following the title. The body in fact treats a wider field — IVF, splitting and fertilising an ovum, and the selection of hereditary traits — and the mismatch between the narrow title and the wider answer is itself worth a reviewer's eye.
شرع ('prescribed, legislated') is deliberately not mapped onto the five rulings; it states that God laid something down, not what category an act falls into.
